recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It restores the surviving FHIR-34096 performer mapping while respecting later applied decisions that removed author and responsible. Review any non-workflow mappings for MessageHeader.source.sender separately under the later sender-move issues if desired.
issue_request: FHIR-34096 was Published/Persuasive for R5 and asked that MessageHeader be mapped to the Workflow Event pattern, including MessageHeader to Event, event[x] to Event.code, sender/author/responsible to Event.performer.actor, and reason to Event.reason.
initial_application: Commits 36d2d8b693 and ea7d85776d initially applied the Event workflow mapping to MessageHeader, event[x], sender, author, responsible, and reason. Current source retained the resource, event[x], and reason mappings, but the surviving sender concept no longer had an Event.performer.actor mapping.
additional_context: Later applied MessageHeader decisions, especially FHIR-41269 and FHIR-32403, moved sender to MessageHeader.source.sender and removed author and responsible for R6. Commit 21db7ce856 applied that refactor and changed Event.performer.actor to unmapped; FHIR-41266 also changed sender wording from system to entity. MessageHeader remains active in source/fhir.ini, and targeted Zulip/Confluence searches found no conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: Added a workflow mapping from MessageHeader.source.sender to Event.performer.actor in source/messageheader/structuredefinition-MessageHeader.xml and updated source/messageheader/messageheader-event-mapping-exceptions.xml so Event.performer.actor is a divergent mapping to MessageHeader.source.sender instead of an unmapped Event pattern element.
source_changes: source/messageheader/structuredefinition-MessageHeader.xml: added workflow mapping Event.performer.actor to MessageHeader.source.sender.
source/messageheader/messageheader-event-mapping-exceptions.xml: replaced the unmapped Event.performer.actor exception with a divergent mapping to MessageHeader.source.sender.
